title: Tolerance is not a virtue.
summary: The final Nietzsche episode of NH's 'Educated Barbarian' series (Beyond Good and Evil). He argues that modern tolerance is a passive way to buy a 'good conscience' rather than real virtue shown through action, and a product of slave morality that breeds mediocrity. He calls for a return to master morality, with virtue coming from strength and the series moving on to Jung next.
claims: Tolerance has become the cardinal virtue of the age, ranked above strength, courage and honesty
Per Nietzsche, every elevation of the human type came from aristocratic societies with gradations of rank, at the cost of things like slavery
Aristocracies fall when rule passes by blood instead of strength, as with pre-revolutionary French nobles; he expects a similar revolt against today's ruling class
Domination still exists, but rank is now measured in money rather than strength of arms
Tolerance is passive and costs nothing, so it buys a 'good conscience' without making you a good person
Whenever society agrees as one on an idea, question it so you aren't just following the crowd
Real virtue is 'morality as attitude', virtue embodied in costly action like giving to a homeless person expecting nothing, versus merely feeling bad for them
As a 5-6 year old, his grandmother let him choose between keeping her leftover shopping money or giving it to homeless people; mostly he gave, and it shaped his adult charity
Virtue is taught by example, not lectures
People who advertise their goodness, like influencers filming donations, are usually lacking virtue
Self-restraint is only a sacrifice for someone who has the power to command; for others, tolerance sacrifices nothing
Master morality judges noble vs despicable; slave morality judges good vs evil and needs the group to validate one's worth
A strong man never asks for his existence to be validated; only he can determine his own validity
Under master morality, charity comes from a superabundance of power rather than pity
Today we live in the most moral age, yet people have never been worse to one another because real virtue has died
Hard times create strong men, strong men create easy times, easy times create weak men; we are now in the 'weak men create hard times' phase
The solution is to embrace master morality again, accept the darkness within yourself, and only then strive to become good
Reading Beyond Good and Evil will change your life; his videos cover only 45-50% of it
